comparison: Perfect agreement on genetic association between KCNK16 L114P and MODY (C2, C19, C21, C24). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing and well-supported by independent family studies and functional characterization.

Complete agreement on genetic background-dependent lethality and survival phenotypes (C3, C37, C38, C116, C117, C118). Both accept the chi-square analysis and survival data, though peer review notes breeding complexity.

Strong agreement on neonatal diabetes mechanism involving insulin secretion defects (C4, C40, C41, C43, C46). OpenEval includes additional claims (C48, C114) about calcium imaging and KCl rescue. Peer review also includes insulin rescue (C5, C11, C49) in this evaluation.

OpenEval focuses specifically on insulin rescue experiment (C5, C49) as separate finding, while peer review groups this with broader neonatal diabetes mechanism. Both find evidence convincing for insulin deficiency causing lethality.

Both address transient neonatal diabetes (C42, C102), but OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED while peer review extends to clinical screening recommendations (C103, C189, C190) also as SUPPORTED. OpenEval treats clinical recommendations separately as UNCERTAIN (R19).

Strong agreement on adult MODY-like phenotype with glucose intolerance and insulin secretion defects (C8, C9, C50, C51, C52, C62, C65). OpenEval includes additional mechanistic claims (C105), both find evidence well-supported.
Perfect agreement on elevated glucagon secretion and fasting hyperglycemia (C53, C54, C66, C67, C140, C186). Both accept the mechanistic interpretation linking glucagon to hepatic glucose production.

Strong agreement on islet composition changes with increased α-cell area and modest β-cell reduction (C68, C69, C106, C148). OpenEval includes neonatal data (C45), both treat morphometric findings as supporting functional defects.

Agreement on electrophysiological findings showing hyperpolarization and increased K+ currents (C71, C72, C74). Peer review groups with broader mechanism (C6, C7), both accept the gain-of-function phenotype.

Agreement on modest current increases in native β-cells versus heterologous expression (C75, C157, C160). Peer review includes additional mechanistic interpretation (C158, C161), both find this discrepancy important for understanding endogenous regulation.

OpenEval evaluates HEK293T overexpression data showing dramatic current increases (C76, C156) as separate finding. Peer review does not separately evaluate this but accepts it as part of broader electrophysiological characterization.

Agreement on sex-specific differences in calcium responses and glucose tolerance (C77, C78, C131, C134). Both find sexual dimorphism well-supported and clinically significant, though peer review emphasizes this as a study strength.

Strong agreement on calcium imaging findings including oscillations and KCl rescue (C82, C83, C84, C85). Both accept that KCl can bypass the membrane potential defect, demonstrating intact calcium machinery.

Agreement on enhanced IP3-induced ER calcium release (C87, C88). OpenEval includes inference about ER localization (C81, C86), peer review explicitly notes consistency with previous TALK-1 ER studies. Both find dual localization supported.

Agreement on RNA sequencing findings showing altered gene expression (C89, C172, C174, C175 in OpenEval; C89, C92, C93, C95-C98 in peer review). Both accept transcriptomic changes as supporting islet dysfunction, though note functional significance is speculative.
OpenEval separately evaluates liraglutide negative result (C91) as SUPPORTED. Peer review does not separately address this finding but accepts overall characterization of cAMP pathway changes.

Both address stress/fibrosis/inflammation gene expression changes (C95, C96, C97, C98). OpenEval notes inference about hyperglycemia causality is not directly tested; peer review accepts as contributing to islet dysfunction.

OpenEval groups main conclusions (C10, C11, C70, C101, C153) as SUPPORTED. Peer review addresses these claims across multiple evaluations, particularly R5 for MODY-like phenotype. Both find overall conclusions well-supported.

Divergence on clinical screening recommendations (C103, C190). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of human neonatal cases; peer review evaluates as SUPPORTED with important clinical implications. Different thresholds for clinical translation.

Divergence on therapeutic implications (C12, C104, C108, C191). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN lacking proof-of-concept experiments; peer review evaluates as SUPPORTED, accepting therapeutic potential as logical extension. Different standards for speculative claims.

Both address sex differences and body composition (C56, C57, C58). OpenEval notes C59 about lean mass causality is speculative; peer review accepts sex differences broadly. Partial overlap with R12 on sexual dimorphism.
Perfect agreement on normal insulin sensitivity from insulin tolerance tests (C63, C64). Both treat this as important control localizing defect to pancreatic islets rather than peripheral tissues.
Agreement on preserved body weight and pancreas mass (C39, C44, C55, C183). Both accept this negative data as ruling out developmental or mass-related explanations for phenotype.
OpenEval separately evaluates lipid measurements showing no differences (C61) as SUPPORTED. Peer review does not separately address this finding but accepts overall metabolic characterization.

OpenEval evaluates reduced somatostatin expression and paracrine signaling hypothesis (C142, C143, C144, C145) as SUPPORTED but notes mechanistic link is indirect. Peer review does not separately evaluate this finding.

Both address discrepancy between heterologous and native expression (C161, C162, C163, C165). OpenEval emphasizes endogenous regulators and correlation with modest phenotype; peer review accepts as important mechanistic insight about limitations.

OpenEval separately evaluates β-cell heterogeneity (C73) as SUPPORTED. Peer review does not separately address this but accepts overall electrophysiological characterization showing variable responses.

Both address dual plasma membrane and ER effects (C167, C168, C169). OpenEval notes relative contributions not quantified; peer review emphasizes consistency with previous ER localization studies. Both find dual localization supported.

Both address adolescent onset matching human MODY (C115, C125, C126, C127). OpenEval emphasizes temporal progression; peer review accepts MODY-like phenotype broadly. Both find model validity well-supported.

OpenEval evaluates genetic background effects and phenotypic variability (C128, C129, C130) as SUPPORTED. Peer review acknowledges breeding complexity but does not separately evaluate genetic modifier hypothesis.
